scope: Theorem 3.5 (Metric inputs) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the fixed subcritical parameter, the LQG metric Dh is a continuous length metric inducing the Euclidean topology. In whole-plane GFF coordinates it is proper and geodesic, and geodesics between each fixed pair of distinct points are almost surely unique. Internal metrics are local in the field. Conformal covariance and Weyl scaling hold: adding a continuous function f multiplies path length locally by eξf . For a compact set K in an ordinary field chart and 0 < χ < ξ(Q − 2), there are almost surely finite random constants controlling connections between nearby points of K inside Euclidean balls of a fixed multiple of their separation by C|z − w|χ. The corresponding internal diameters of small dyadic squares, with a bounded enlargement still in the chart, have the same type of bound. Fixed boxes of bounded aspect ratio admit access to their flat faces by completion of the internal metric. In whole-plane GFF coordinates, strong confluence holds simultaneously for all geodesics: an interior segment of any geodesic persists in all geodesics whose endpoints sufficiently closely approximate slightly longer interior subsegments. The same local assertion holds for short geodesic subarcs in buffered ordinary surface charts. In particular, every nonempty open geodesic subarc contains a segment of a geodesic between points of a deterministic countable dense set.
